Deployment Runbook - Widget Service v3

Last edited by J. Smith on 2025-09-15 • Page ID: 100101

Overview

This runbook describes the deployment procedure for the Widget Service v3. It covers pre-deployment checks, deployment steps, and rollback procedures. For the Widget Service architecture, see Architecture Overview. For API details, see API Reference.

Pre-Deployment Checklist

Complete all items below before initiating a deployment:

  • CI pipeline passes on the release branch (all stages green).
  • Release candidate Docker image tagged and pushed to registry.
  • Database migrations reviewed and approved by DBA.
  • Feature flags for new features set to disabled in production.
  • On-call engineer notified and available for the deployment window.
  • Rollback procedure reviewed (see Rollback section).

Deployment Steps

Step 1 — Database Migration

Run the migration from the deploy host using the following command:


# Connect to the deploy host
ssh deploy@widget-deploy.internal

# Run database migration
cd /opt/widget-service
uv run alembic upgrade head

# Verify migration completed
uv run alembic current

Step 2 — Rolling Container Update

Trigger the rolling update via the deployment pipeline. The Kubernetes deployment uses RollingUpdate strategy with maxUnavailable: 0 and maxSurge: 1 to ensure zero-downtime deployment. 


# Tag the release
git tag -s v3.2.1 -m "Release v3.2.1 — improved throughput"
git push origin v3.2.1

# Trigger the deployment pipeline
gh workflow run deploy.yml -f environment=production -f version=v3.2.1

# Monitor the rollout
kubectl rollout status deployment/widget-service -n production --timeout=10m

Step 3 — Smoke Tests

After deployment, run the smoke test suite to verify basic functionality:


# smoke_test.py — run against production endpoint
import httpx

BASE_URL = "https://api.widget.acme.example/v3"

def test_health():
    r = httpx.get(f"{BASE_URL}/health")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.json()["status"] == "ok"

def test_widget_list():
    r = httpx.get(f"{BASE_URL}/widgets", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer $TOKEN"})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert "items" in r.json()

Rollback Procedure

If the deployment fails or post-deployment smoke tests fail, roll back immediately. Do not attempt to fix forward during a production incident. 


# Roll back to the previous deployment
kubectl rollout undo deployment/widget-service -n production

# Verify rollback completed
kubectl rollout status deployment/widget-service -n production

# If database migration must be reversed:
uv run alembic downgrade -1

Widget Service Architecture Overview

Last edited by A. Chen on 2025-09-01 • Page ID: 100001

System Components

The Widget Service consists of three main components. For deployment instructions, see Deployment Runbook. For the API contract, see API Reference.

  • API Gateway - handles authentication, rate limiting, routing.
  • Widget Service - core business logic; stateless; scalable.
  • Widget Database — PostgreSQL 16; primary with one read replica.

Data Flow

All client requests enter via the API Gateway over HTTPS (TLS 1.3 required). The gateway validates the JWT token, applies rate limits (100 req/min per token by default), and routes to the Widget Service. The Widget Service never writes directly to the replica; reads are routed to the replica for non-transactional queries.

Configuration Reference

Setting Env Var Default Description
Database URL WIDGET_DB_URL (required) PostgreSQL connection string for the primary database.
Replica URL WIDGET_DB_REPLICA_URL same as primary Optional read-replica URL. Falls back to primary if not set.
Rate limit WIDGET_RATE_LIMIT 100 Requests per minute per API token.
Log level WIDGET_LOG_LEVEL INFO Python logging level: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR.
CORS origins WIDGET_CORS_ORIGINS * Comma-separated list of allowed origins. Use * to allow all (dev only).

Kubernetes Resource Allocation


# widget-service deployment resource spec
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: 250m
    memory: 512Mi
  limits:
    cpu: 1000m
    memory: 1Gi

# Horizontal Pod Autoscaler
minReplicas: 2
maxReplicas: 10
targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 70
